nd3f74ee9998.s: Pushpabhadraswami and Ashtabhuja Narayana, among the earliest Hindu temples in Andhra, are located at:
nd3f74ee9998.x: Both shrines stand at Nagarjunakonda and are counted among the Ikshvaku-period firsts as the earliest Hindu temples in Andhra.

n78ec40c44da.s: Which Ikshvaku ruler performed the Ashvamedha, Vajapeya and Rajasuya, corroborated by an Ashvamedha platform at Nagarjunakonda?
n78ec40c44da.x: Vasishthiputra Chamtamula performed the Ashvamedha, Vajapeya, Agnishtoma and Rajasuya; the Ashvamedha platform at Nagarjunakonda is the evidence.

n78136c07e20.s: The Ikshvakus of Andhra were initially feudatories of the:
n78136c07e20.x: The Ikshvakus began as feudatories of the Satavahanas, as the Alluru record shows.

n44bcd94b3ef.s: The first Sanskrit inscriptions in the Telugu lands belong to the reign of:
n44bcd94b3ef.x: Ehuvala Chamtamula, son of Virapurushadatta, issued the first Sanskrit inscriptions in the Telugu lands; the Gummadidurru inscription is also his.

nab247808c4f.s: An Ashvamedha altar associated with the sacrifices of Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula has been found at:
nab247808c4f.x: Santamula performed the Ashvamedha, Vajapeya and Agnistoma, and an Ashvamedha altar has been found at Nagarjunakonda.

n8156281534b.s: Under the Ikshvakus, which varna constituted the majority of society?
n8156281534b.x: Shudras formed the majority under the Ikshvakus, while Brahmins benefited from Brahmadeya grants and a new landlord class emerged.

ne99dd9657fd.s: Under the Ikshvakus, the major patrons of Buddhism at Nagarjunakonda were the:
ne99dd9657fd.x: The Ikshvaku kings were Vedic in orientation, while queens and royal women patronised Buddhism, making donations without male intervention.

nb69aab8831f.s: Cross-cousin marriage with a maternal uncle's daughter began with which dynasty?
nb69aab8831f.x: Cross-cousin marriage began with the Ikshvakus; Virapurushadatta married his aunts' daughters.

n129fdb5213a.s: Royal names such as 'Vasishthiputra' in Ikshvaku inscriptions are examples of:
n129fdb5213a.x: Ikshvaku kings used matronymics such as Vasishthiputra, naming themselves after their mothers.

n1214eaf273c.s: Ikshvaku coins were mainly made of:
n1214eaf273c.x: Ikshvaku coins were of lead and copper and bore the Ujjain symbol, the elephant and the lion.

n9a39d7b6e72.s: Chamtisri built or restored the Maha Chaitya at Nagarjunakonda in which regnal year of Virapurushadatta?
n9a39d7b6e72.x: Chamtisri, sister of Sri Santamula and paternal aunt of Virapurushadatta, built or restored the Maha Chaitya in his sixth regnal year.

n2521272ddbc.s: Who is regarded as the first woman donor at Nagarjunakonda?
n2521272ddbc.x: Chamtisri, sister of Sri Santamula, was the first woman donor; Bodhisri is ranked first among women donors for the extent of her service.

n5af19849967.s: The Paravata Mahachaitya, later rebuilt by Chamtisri, had been built by Yajnasri Satakarni for:
n5af19849967.x: The earlier Paravata Mahachaitya was built by Yajnasri Satakarni for Acharya Nagarjuna; Chamtisri rebuilt it in Virapurushadatta's sixth year.

n5fa0a940e5c.s: Which Ikshvaku ruler built a vihara for the Bahushrutiyas in his mother's name?
n5fa0a940e5c.x: Ehuvala Santamula combined a revival of Brahmanism with Buddhist patronage, building a vihara for the Bahushrutiyas in his mother's name.

n97337a33aa2.s: Bodhisri's Sinhala Vihara at Nagarjunakonda belonged to which Buddhist sect?
n97337a33aa2.x: Bodhisri's Sinhala Vihara belonged to the Mahaviharavasins; the Maha Chaitya was Aparamahavinaseliya and Kodabalisri's vihara Mahishasaka.

nap-history-7-17.s: The Kumara Swami temple at Nagarjunakonda was built by the Ikshvaku commander:
nap-history-7-17.x: Kumara Swami was the deity of the temple built by the Ikshvaku commander Elisiri; Shivasena was a commander of the Abhira king Vasusena.

n744b035ac5e.s: The Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami shrine at Nagarjunakonda, the first Vaishnava temple in Andhra, was built by:
n744b035ac5e.x: Shivasena, commander of the Abhira king Vasusena, built the Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami (Vishnu) shrine.

nba18efe93ea.s: How many Shaiva temples stood at Nagarjunakonda alongside its single Vaishnava temple?
nba18efe93ea.x: Nagarjunakonda had nine Shaiva temples and one Vaishnava temple (Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami), ten in all.

n8406c1e2b06.s: The tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus, at whose shrine women offered bangles, was:
n8406c1e2b06.x: Hariti (Harati), protector of children, was the Ikshvaku tutelary deity; women offered bangles at her shrine, and her image marks the beginning of Shakti worship.

n2bc5eca95db.s: Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula worshipped which deities as his family deities?
n2bc5eca95db.x: Sri Santamula worshipped Virupakshapati (Shiva) and Mahasena (Kartikeya) and granted agraharas to northern Brahmins.

n00c42f24304.s: The Pushpabhadraswami (Shiva) shrine at Nagarjunakonda followed which plan?
n00c42f24304.x: The Pushpabhadraswami shrine had a Gajaprishtha plan; it was begun by Virapurushadatta and completed by Ehuvala.

n167f21db7da.s: Upasika Bodhisri built seven viharas at:
n167f21db7da.x: Bodhisri built seven viharas at Papili, besides viharas for monks from Sinhala, Kashmir, China and Gandhara.

ne230abcd224.s: Sriparvataswami, the family deity of the Vishnukundins, is identified with:
ne230abcd224.x: The Vishnukundin family deity Sriparvataswami is identified with Mallikarjuna of Srisailam.

nap-history-7-15.s: The Pedavegi inscription recording a land grant to Vishnu belongs to the Salankayana king:
nap-history-7-15.x: The Pedavegi inscription of the Salankayana king Nandivarman II records a land grant to Vishnu.

nap-history-6-18.s: Temples of Harati, Mahajana, Kumara Swami and Pushpabhadra Swami were discovered in excavations at:
nap-history-6-18.x: All of these, along with Ashtabhuja Narayana Swami, were found in the Nagarjunakonda excavations.

nap-history-7-3.s: The term 'Bappa Bhattaraka', associated with the Salankayanas, means:
nap-history-7-3.x: The Salankayanas called themselves devotees of Bappa Bhattaraka, a term meaning regarding the father as God.

na0c185edbe2.s: Under which dynasty did royal patronage of Buddhism in Andhra reach its last zenith?
na0c185edbe2.x: The Ikshvakus represented the last royal Buddhist zenith in Andhra; their period also saw the first Vaishnava temple, Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami.

ne00334b5cfc.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched (sculpture at Nagarjunakonda)?
o: Nagarjunakonda – main centre of the Gandhara School
Later Ikshvaku phase – Buddha shown only through symbols
Final mature phase of the Amaravati School – Satavahanas
ne00334b5cfc.x: The mature phase under the Ikshvakus followed Mahayana themes; Nagarjunakonda was a centre of the Amaravati School, which reached its final phase under the Ikshvakus, and the Buddha then appeared in human form.

nca00aa38928.s: The Mandhata sculpture, the first depiction of a Chakravarti in Indian art, is found at:
nca00aa38928.x: The Mandhata sculpture at Jaggayyapeta, the most important Ikshvaku sculpture, is the first depiction of a Chakravarti in Indian art.

nd9314b15ab5.s: Early Ikshvaku carving is described as the 'last flicker' of the:
nd9314b15ab5.x: Early Ikshvaku carving, with less stylisation and low relief, is called the last flicker of the Satavahana Amaravati tradition.

n6999aacb516.s: The first sculptor signatures and the first structural Hindu temples are associated with which dynasty?
n6999aacb516.x: The Ikshvakus are credited with the first sculptor signatures, the first structural Hindu temples and the first Sanskrit inscription in South India.

n1a05d14422c.s: Ayaka platforms are architectural features associated with:
n1a05d14422c.x: Ayaka platforms belong to stupas; the Agamic temple plan comprises garbhagudi, antarala, mantapa, dhvajastambha and prakara.

n79c6ca08531.s: The major stupas at Nagarjunakonda were built on a ____ plan with Ayaka platforms in four directions.
n79c6ca08531.x: The major stupas had a wheel-shaped or spoked plan with Ayaka platforms in the four directions.

n07e82514502.s: Indrapalanagara, the Vishnukundin capital of Madhava Varma I and Govinda Varma, is identified with:
n07e82514502.x: Indrapalanagara, built by Indravarma, is Tummalagudem in Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri (Nalgonda), Telangana; Denduluru was a later capital.

n9c10ed05247.s: Which is regarded as the first Sanskrit inscription found in Telangana?
n9c10ed05247.x: The Tummalagudem plates, recording a grant to Paramabhattarika's vihara, are regarded as the first Sanskrit inscription found in Telangana.

nd160775e0a7.s: Pulakeshin II ended Vishnukundin rule by defeating Manchana Bhattaraka at Kunala (Kolleru) in:
nd160775e0a7.x: Pulakeshin II defeated Manchana Bhattaraka at Kunala near Kolleru in 624 CE; his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana then founded the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi.

ncd2f6273412.s: Govinda Varma's Chaitanyapuri record, unlike most Vishnukundin inscriptions, was written in:
ncd2f6273412.x: Of the 21 Vishnukundin inscriptions (16 copper-plate, 5 stone), Govinda Varma's Chaitanyapuri record was in Prakrit.

n371c56506c3.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler bore the title 'Satyasraya'?
n371c56506c3.x: Indrabhattaraka Varma was Satyasraya; Govinda Varma was Shadabhigna and Vikramendra Varma I was Mahakavi.

n0f03bef60eb.s: The Telugu phrase 'Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul' occurs in the:
n0f03bef60eb.x: The Chikkulla plates of Vikramendra Varma II carry the Telugu phrase 'Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul'.

n02658bdf7a2.s: The Vishnukundin king Indrabhattaraka Varma was defeated by the Maukhari ruler:
n02658bdf7a2.x: Indrabhattaraka Varma was defeated by Maukhari Ishanavarma and was killed in the Kalinga war.

nc2dc66b2ca4.s: The capital of the Salankayanas was:
nc2dc66b2ca4.x: The Salankayana capital was Vengi, identified with Pedavegi in Eluru district; they followed Vaishnavism and were conquered by Madhava Varma II.

n59faf74a300.s: Madhava Varma I is credited with excavating cave temples at Undavalli, Bhairavakona and:
n59faf74a300.x: Madhava Varma I, who ruled for 22 years, is associated with the caves at Undavalli, Bhairavakona and Mogalrajapuram.

n5f990147e27.s: The grant of Irundhera was made by the Vishnukundin ruler:
n5f990147e27.x: Vikramendra Varma II granted Irundhera; Govinda Varma I founded the Govinda Vihara and his queen the Paramabhattarika Mahadevi Vihara.

n8dc060b89d8.s: In Vishnukundin administration, 'Vishti' (later 'vetti' in Telugu) referred to:
n8dc060b89d8.x: Vishti was forced labour, later called vetti in Telugu; Bhaga was the one-sixth share of produce.

n0e0b240778e.s: The Tundi plates of the Vishnukundins record the grant of Tundi village to the scholar:
n0e0b240778e.x: The Tundi plates record the gift of Tundi village to Shivavarma; the Ipur plates name Agnisarma and Easwarasarma as donees.

n4eb14750e0d.s: Janasraya Chhandovichiti, credited to Madhava Varma II, is a Sanskrit work on:
n4eb14750e0d.x: Janasraya Chhandovichiti is a Sanskrit work on prosody, credited to Madhava Varma II (title Janasraya), though some attribute it to the poet Gunaswami.

o: Iron with a thin coating of copper
n1c104c774a6.x: Vishnukundin coins were of iron with a thin copper coating; Rayaprolu Subrahmanyam brought them to light and 16 types are known.

n13bb487ec76.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Undavalli caves?
o: They are situated in Guntur district on the Krishna.
They are a Vishnukundina adaptation of the Gupta rock-cut style.
They contain a five-metre reclining image of Ananta Padmanabha Vishnu.
They were built by the Cholas.
n13bb487ec76.x: Undavalli is a Vishnukundin cave of the 4th-5th century CE; the Cholas did not build it. The other three statements are correct.

nb4d7ba66987.s: How many rock-cut caves are there at Bhairavakonda?
nb4d7ba66987.x: Bhairavakonda has eight rock-cut Shiva caves, a Kapalika Shaiva centre with lion pedestals and kumbha capitals.

ndff0a54ef4c.s: The Undavalli caves, with a monolithic reclining Ananta Padmanabha Swamy, are situated on the bank of the:
ndff0a54ef4c.x: The Undavalli caves are a Vishnukundin monument on the bank of the Krishna containing a monolithic reclining Ananta Padmanabha Swamy.

n40eef71c738.s: Vishnukundin rock-cut caves are generally dated to the:
n40eef71c738.x: The Vishnukundin caves belong to the 4th-6th centuries (Undavalli 4th-5th), earlier than Mahendravarman I's 7th-century Pallava caves.

na500ce61b1a.s: Some sources credit Madhava Varma I with the Bhairavakonda caves; another dates them to the period of the:
na500ce61b1a.x: Some sources credit the Vishnukundin Madhava Varma I, while another dates Bhairavakonda to the Pallava period of the 7th-8th centuries CE.

nb6e7d0f17d0.s: The Undavalli caves were first used as a:
nb6e7d0f17d0.x: Undavalli was first a Jain abode, then used by Buddhist monks, and later converted into a Hindu temple.

n77e09d0cad6.s: The Undavalli caves, carved from the top downward, have how many storeys?
n77e09d0cad6.x: Undavalli has four storeys with three main caves; the upper levels are finely detailed while the ground floor is crude and unfinished.

n24e1d6493c1.s: The union of a lower-caste man with a higher-caste woman was termed:
n24e1d6493c1.x: Viloma (Pratiloma) was the union of a lower-caste man with a higher-caste woman, whose offspring was termed Chandala; Anuloma was the reverse.

nap-history-45-17.s: 'Samayamu' during the Kakatiya period referred to:
nap-history-45-17.x: Samayamu were caste associations of the Kakatiya period; Kayasthas were the record-keepers.

nc875e20718f.s: The amphitheatre at Nagarjunakonda (Vijayapuri) was used mainly for:
nc875e20718f.x: The amphitheatre at the Ikshvaku capital Vijayapuri was for performances and games, not Vedic sacrifices.

nfb3da07bd6a.s: Which Satavahana inscription refers to Brahmins trained in Vedic learning and rituals?
nfb3da07bd6a.x: The Nanaghat inscription mentions Brahmins trained in Vedic learning and ritual; Satavahana kings enforced varna-dharma and gave tax-free villages to Brahmins.

nf3c52a1d5ce.s: In early Andhra society, the sub-caste 'Selavaddikas' were:
nf3c52a1d5ce.x: Selavaddikas were stone sculptors or masons; Halikas were farmers, Sethis merchants and Swarnakaras goldsmiths.

na70fe75486c.s: Under the Vishnukundins, which group was regarded as 'the backbone' of society and received land grants?
na70fe75486c.x: Farmers were called the backbone and received land grants; Vaisyas carried on trade and artisans such as carpenters and weavers had a recognised place.

n45770835f85.s: Besides building and repairing viharas, the Vishnukundins patronised which Shiva temple?
n45770835f85.x: The Vishnukundins, titled Paramamaheswara and Parama Brahmanya, patronised the Ramalingeswara Shiva temple and also built and repaired viharas.

n8c6a16316b0.s: Which literary work mentions inter-caste marriages, showing that caste was not completely rigid in the early period?
n8c6a16316b0.x: Kathasaritsagara mentions inter-caste marriages, showing that caste practice was not completely rigid at that stage.

n40a7f06e78b.s: In the reliefs of Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda, men are typically shown wearing a lower cloth and a:
n40a7f06e78b.x: The reliefs show men in a lower cloth with a turban, while women wear heavy anklets, bangles, girdles and necklaces.

n912cd994fcd.s: Ikshvaku kings performed Vedic sacrifices, while Ikshvaku queens patronised:
n912cd994fcd.x: Ikshvaku religious life was split: kings performed Vedic sacrifices and queens patronised Buddhism.

nfad55407200.s: Gautami Balasri, the Satavahana royal woman patron, funded a cave-vihara at:
nfad55407200.x: Gautami Balasri funded a cave-vihara at Nasik; she was a patron, not one of the women poets of the Gathasaptasati.

n6b0c1bd0889.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sangam corpus?
o: Ettuthogai and Pattupattu together form the Melkanakku, the eighteen major works.
Pathinenkilkanakku is older than the Ettuthogai and Pattupattu.
Pathinenkilkanakku is a set of eighteen minor works on ethics.
The Tirukkural is part of the Pathinenkilkanakku.
n6b0c1bd0889.x: Pathinenkilkanakku is largely post-Sangam, so it is not older than Ettuthogai and Pattupattu; the other statements are correct.

na9ce97f1650.s: According to tradition, the second Sangam was held at:
na9ce97f1650.x: Tradition places the first Sangam at Then Madurai, the second at Kapatapuram and the third at Madurai, all under Pandya patronage.

ndcacda52711.s: The Sangams were assemblies of poets held under the patronage of the:
ndcacda52711.x: The Sangams were held under Pandya patronage; the corpus has about 2,400 poems by several hundred poets.

n93c91dd601f.s: Ettuthogai and Pattupattu poems are divided into which two themes?
n93c91dd601f.x: Sangam poems are divided into aham (love, interior) and puram (war and public life) themes.

n9d0a5b4e3cb.s: In the Tirukkural, the book 'Porul' deals with:
n9d0a5b4e3cb.x: The Tirukkural's 1,330 couplets are in three books: Aram (virtue), Porul (wealth) and Inbam (love).

ncde45732ad2.s: Sangam literature was composed in Tamil, whereas the contemporary Satavahanas used:
ncde45732ad2.x: The contemporary Satavahanas used Prakrit, in contrast to the Tamil of Sangam literature.

nindian-history-13-4.s: The oldest extant Tamil grammar is:
nindian-history-13-4.x: Tolkappiyam, dealing with grammar and poetics, is the oldest surviving Tamil grammar.

n8b7eb8b6d7a.s: Which Ettuthogai anthology is associated with the Chera kings?
n8b7eb8b6d7a.x: Padirruppattu is the Ettuthogai anthology on the Chera kings; the other three belong to Pattupattu.

n0a3792c63f9.s: In Manimekalai, the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi becomes a:
n0a3792c63f9.x: Manimekalai tells how the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi becomes a Buddhist nun, and reflects Buddhist philosophy.

ndf55074cfde.s: Which Chola king won the battles of Venni and Vahaipparandalai?
ndf55074cfde.x: Karikala Chola won at Venni and Vahaipparandalai, reclaimed forest land and is the subject of Pattinappalai.

ne593c7eb791.s: In Sangam polity, the title 'Enadi' was given to:
ne593c7eb791.x: Enadi was the title of army commanders; minor hill and forest chieftains were the Velir, and Avai was the royal court.

nindian-history-15-11.s: Naura, Tondi, Mushiri (Muziris) and Nelisanda were western-coast Sangam ports mainly in the ____ country.
nindian-history-15-11.x: All four were major western-coast ports of the Sangam age, mainly in the Chera country.

n6a77562d075.s: Pari, Kari, Ori, Pegan, Ay, Athiyaman and Nalli are collectively known as the:
n6a77562d075.x: These seven were the Kadai ezhu vallals, the seven great patrons; Pandya rulers such as Nedunjeliyan were not among them.

nd80a221db0a.s: The capital of the Sangam Cholas was:
nd80a221db0a.x: The Chola capital was Uraiyur, its port Puhar (Kaveripattinam) and emblem the tiger; Korkai was the Pandya port.

n91cf90e6d8c.s: In Sangam tradition, Nalli is remembered as one of the:
n91cf90e6d8c.x: Nalli was one of the seven great patrons (Kadai ezhu vallals), not a minister of the Aimperunkulu.

n63e3cb34d67.s: Which dynasty rose only from the fourth century CE, after the Sangam age?
n63e3cb34d67.x: The Pallavas rose from the fourth century CE; the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas were the three Sangam dynasties.

n5c61922e949.s: In the Sangam tradition, stones erected in memory of warriors who died in battle were called:
n5c61922e949.x: Nadukal (hero stones) commemorated fallen warriors, often carved with their deeds and sometimes inscribed.

n1e26a3db65e.s: Indo-Roman trade in the southern peninsula peaked broadly between the:
n1e26a3db65e.x: Indo-Roman trade peaked in the Satavahana-Sangam age, broadly 1st century BCE to 2nd century CE, and declined after the Satavahanas.

n291f22eebd0.s: The Tolkappiyam lists four social groups: Arasar, Anthanar, Vanigar and ____.
n291f22eebd0.x: Tolkappiyam lists Arasar, Anthanar, Vanigar and Vellalar, with Vellalar fourth; rigid varna had not yet developed.

nc0dc6cc63a0.s: Arikamedu, the foremost Indo-Roman trading station on the east coast, was excavated by Mortimer Wheeler in:
nc0dc6cc63a0.x: Wheeler excavated Arikamedu, near Puducherry, in 1945, finding Roman amphorae, Arretine ware, rouletted ware and Tamil-Brahmi sherds.

naf96318908d.s: Which period is often called the 'dark age' of Tamil history?
naf96318908d.x: The Kalabhra period was called a dark age because later Brahmanical records portrayed the Kalabhras as evil and sources are scarce.

n2cd07440107.s: In Indo-Roman trade, 'Yavanapriya' ('beloved of the Yavanas') referred to:
n2cd07440107.x: Yavanapriya was black pepper, Rome's most prized Indian import; muslin and ivory were also exports, while gold, horses and wine came in.

n7f3f2b8457a.s: Which of the following was a woman poet of the Sangam age?
n7f3f2b8457a.x: Avvaiyar, like Nachchellaiyar and Kakkaipadiniyar, was a Sangam woman poet.

nindian-history-26-2-12.s: Muziris (Mushiri) was the chief port of the:
nindian-history-26-2-12.x: Muziris was the chief Chera port; Korkai was Pandya, Puhar Chola and Motupalli Kakatiya.

nindian-history-26-13.s: Motupalli, known for its trade inscription, was a seaport of the:
nindian-history-26-13.x: Motupalli was a Kakatiya port in Andhra; the major Chola port was Puhar (Kaveripattinam).

n38b754e5ed8.s: The Kalabhras are described as patrons of:
n38b754e5ed8.x: The Kalabhras patronised Jainism and Buddhism rather than Vedic Brahmanism.

n6007567edc9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Samudragupta's campaigns?
o: The Ganga-Yamuna region in the north was directly annexed.
The southern rulers were defeated and reinstated as tributaries.
Assam, Nepal and Bengal were directly annexed to the empire.
The atavika (forest) kingdoms of central India were subdued.
n6007567edc9.x: Assam, Nepal and Bengal were frontier rulers who paid tribute, not annexed territories; the other three statements are correct.

n226e3e7cf0f.s: Meghavarman of Sri Lanka sent a mission to Samudragupta seeking permission to build a monastery at:
n226e3e7cf0f.x: A Chinese source records Meghavarman's request to build a monastery at Bodh Gaya.

n8d2e079960d.s: Who called Samudragupta the 'Napoleon of India'?
n8d2e079960d.x: V.A. Smith called Samudragupta the Napoleon of India; the Allahabad prashasti calls him Lichchhavi-dauhitra.

n59ff2b8bb02.s: How many southern kings did Samudragupta defeat and reinstate in his Dakshinapatha campaign?
n59ff2b8bb02.x: Twelve kings between the Ganga and the Kaveri were captured and reinstated under the grahana-moksha-anugraha policy; there was no annexation in the south.

nindian-history-1-15.s: The Bhitari pillar inscription records the war of which Gupta ruler with the Hunas?
nindian-history-1-15.x: The Bhitari pillar records Skandagupta's war with the Hunas.

n8ecd9eb68ab.s: The Devichandraguptam, narrating the Ramagupta-Dhruvadevi episode, was written by:
n8ecd9eb68ab.x: Vishakhadatta wrote both the Devichandraguptam and the Mudrarakshasa, a drama on Chanakya and Chandragupta Maurya.

nb97a61be215.x: Kuberanaga was the queen of Chandragupta II; Kumaradevi, Duttadevi and Anantadevi were queens of Chandragupta I, Samudragupta and Kumaragupta I.

nd342e0d7679.s: Harisena, of Samudragupta's court, held the offices of Kumaramatya, Sandhivigrahika and:
nd342e0d7679.x: Harisena was Kumaramatya, Sandhivigrahika and Mahadandanayaka; he is distinct from the later Jain author of the Brihatkatha Kosha.

nbd705251bd5.s: The Mandsaur inscription is associated with:
nbd705251bd5.x: Vatsabhatti composed the Mandsaur inscription; Virasena is linked with Udayagiri.

n90ffa1da7fc.s: The first Gupta ruler to assume the title 'Maharajadhiraja' was:
n90ffa1da7fc.x: Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha used Maharaja; Chandragupta I first adopted Maharajadhiraja.

nindian-history-1-70.s: Samudragupta's Prayag Prashasti, composed in Sanskrit by Harisena, is written in which script?
nindian-history-1-70.x: Harisena's Prayag Prashasti is a Sanskrit panegyric of Samudragupta inscribed in Brahmi.

nb06372e42c0.s: Chandragupta I married Kumaradevi, a princess of the:
nb06372e42c0.x: Chandragupta I married the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi and issued the first Gupta gold coins of the king-queen type.

nbeab6c71d21.s: Which powers paid homage to the Gupta ruler, while Southeast Asian kings and Ceylon sent tribute?
nbeab6c71d21.x: Kushanas and Sakas paid homage, while rulers of Southeast Asia and Ceylon sent tribute.

n711254a78c5.s: The Allahabad Prasasti of Samudragupta mixes prose and verse in the ____ style.
n711254a78c5.x: The Allahabad (Prayaga) Prasasti is a Sanskrit eulogy combining prose and verse in the champu style.

n83962efb74b.s: The capital of Chandragupta I was:
n83962efb74b.x: Chandragupta I ruled South Bihar and parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh, including Saketa and Prayaga, with Pataliputra as capital.

n7d016cbcd2f.s: Gupta coins, important for royal titles and religious affiliations, were mostly made of:
n7d016cbcd2f.x: Gupta coins, mostly gold, depict rulers, deities and rituals, revealing titles, religion and prosperity.

nindian-history-1-35.s: The Eran inscription of 510 CE, the first epigraphic evidence of sati, records the wife of the commander:
nindian-history-1-35.x: The Eran inscription records that the wife of the commander Goparaja burned herself on his pyre.

nindian-history-82-4.s: Which Mauryan ruler is credited with extending Mauryan power into the Deccan?
nindian-history-82-4.x: Bindusara pushed Mauryan power into the Deccan; Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire.

nindian-history-82-5.s: The Nalanda Mahavihara was founded by:
nindian-history-82-5.x: Kumaragupta I founded Nalanda; Skandagupta resisted the Hunas and Harsha patronised Banabhatta.

ne1d1afc3e15.s: The rise of which of the following powers weakened Gupta authority?
ne1d1afc3e15.x: The rise of the Maukharis, Maitrakas, Later Guptas and Pushyabhutis, along with feudatories fostered by land grants, weakened Gupta authority.

nd4fefb7c891.s: The last ruler of the main Gupta line, c. 540-550 CE, was:
nd4fefb7c891.x: Vishnugupta, ruling about 540-550 CE, was the last ruler of the main Gupta line.

n768bf94cfa1.s: The Maitrakas, who rose during Gupta decline, ruled from:
n768bf94cfa1.x: The Maitrakas were based at Valabhi; the Aulikaras at Mandsaur, the Pushyabhutis at Thanesar and the Later Guptas in Magadha.

ndac6a5af14c.s: According to the Ramagupta episode, Ramagupta agreed to surrender Dhruvadevi to a king of the:
ndac6a5af14c.x: Ramagupta agreed to give Dhruvadevi to a Saka king; Chandragupta II killed the Saka king, then Ramagupta, and married Dhruvadevi.

n2760f3d89bb.s: Chandragupta II annexed western Malwa and Gujarat by defeating the Saka ruler:
n2760f3d89bb.x: Chandragupta II defeated Rudrasimha III, annexed western Malwa and Gujarat, made Ujjain his second capital and issued Saka-model silver coins.

nindian-history-96-1.s: The Gupta era of 319-20 CE was started by:
nindian-history-96-1.x: Chandragupta I started the Gupta era in 319-20 CE.

n0a203d808f8.s: Which Gupta ruler repulsed the Hunas twice and then assumed the title Vikramaditya?
n0a203d808f8.x: Skandagupta repulsed the Hunas twice during his own reign and took the title Vikramaditya.

naa35a5758d8.s: Besides Mahendraditya, Kumaragupta I bore the title:
naa35a5758d8.x: Kumaragupta I was Shakraditya and Mahendraditya; Vikramaditya belongs to Chandragupta II and Skandagupta.

n754604f1dad.s: The title 'Baladitya' is associated with the Gupta ruler:
n754604f1dad.x: Baladitya was Narasimhagupta; Chandragupta II was also known as Devagupta and Devaraja.

n53954e031d1.s: Chandragupta II's daughter Prabhavati Gupta married the Vakataka ruler:
n53954e031d1.x: Prabhavati Gupta married Rudrasena II, an alliance through which Gupta influence extended into the Deccan without annexation.

ne2a70eb8f2d.s: In the later Gupta period, what reduced state revenue and so the ability to maintain a professional army?
ne2a70eb8f2d.x: Land grants reduced the revenue available to the state, making a professional army hard to maintain.

nindian-history-97-4.s: The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of:
nindian-history-97-4.x: Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya), though he never names the king.

n63d44dacd61.s: Which of the following was a major successor power of the Guptas in the north and west?
n63d44dacd61.x: The Maukharis, Maitrakas and Pushyabhutis succeeded the Guptas; the Paramaras of Malwa were a later power.

n592332812fd.s: Which of the following was a cause of the decline of the Gupta Empire?
n592332812fd.x: Huna invasions, along with the growth of feudatories and loss of western trade revenue, caused Gupta decline; the Arab invasion was not a factor.

nd410c2dccc6.s: Compared with the Mauryan Empire, the Gupta Empire was:
nd410c2dccc6.x: Gupta administration relied on feudatories and land grantees, with some hereditary offices, and was less centralised than the Mauryan.

nfa001226b18.s: In the Gupta period, a land grant made to temples and monasteries was called a:
nfa001226b18.x: Devagrahara grants went to temples and monasteries; brahmadeya and agrahara went to Brahmanas and secular grants to officials or feudatories.

n94220cb3cb4.x: Khila was untilled waste land; Kshetra was cultivated land, Vastu house-site land and Aprahata forest land.

nff48b96401b.s: Which of the following was treated as a criminal offence in the Gupta judicial system?
nff48b96401b.x: The Gupta period separated civil and criminal law more clearly: theft and adultery were criminal, property disputes civil.

ne043e83ef18.s: Land grants in tribal and forest regions led absorbed tribal groups to emerge as:
ne043e83ef18.x: Such grants brought virgin land under cultivation and absorbed tribes into the caste order as new sub-castes.

naf694b4e294.s: Unlike the centrally regulated Mauryan state, Gupta administration relied to a greater extent on:
naf694b4e294.x: The Mauryan state was centrally regulated, whereas Gupta administration relied more on feudatories and grantees.

nb97d6646a4a.s: In the Gupta period, peasants increasingly became:
nb97d6646a4a.x: Peasants became semi-servile, with tenant farming, sharecropping, tenancy at will and many taxes.

n9fd8d335dca.s: On the Gupta town board (adhikarana), the Prathama kulika represented the:
n9fd8d335dca.x: The Prathama kulika represented chief artisans; the Nagarashreshthi chaired the board, the Prathama kayastha was chief scribe and the Sarthavaha the caravan trader.

nindian-history-83-14.s: In the ancient Indian revenue system, 'Hiranya' meant:
o: A cash payment instead of produce
nindian-history-83-14.x: Hiranya was a cash payment; Bhaga was the share of produce, Valiam a commodity tax and Sita revenue from crown land.

nindian-history-23-3.s: In the Gupta period, 'Vishti', counted as a source of state income, meant:
nindian-history-23-3.x: Vishti, or forced labour, was treated as a form of tax; tax-free land was granted to Brahmins and religious functionaries.

n9b79a8b5f7b.s: Satavahana and Ikshvaku brahmadeya grants barred ____ from interfering in the granted areas.
n9b79a8b5f7b.x: Brahmadeya grants of the Satavahanas and Ikshvakus barred royal officials from interfering in the granted areas.

n4bdd79d558d.s: Under the Gupta kings, salaries of officials were often paid in:
n4bdd79d558d.x: Gupta kingship was hereditary without firm primogeniture; several offices were hereditary and salaries were often paid in land or kind.

nd4d35876cba.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about society as described by Fa-Hien?
o: Cowrie shells were used in daily exchange.
Hindus and Buddhists lived in harmony.
The people were peaceful and prosperous.
Chandalas followed the same food restrictions as everyone else.
nd4d35876cba.x: The Chandalas were an exception to the general food restrictions; the other three are Fa-Hien's observations.

n46ad554529b.s: During the Gupta period, the Dharmashastras advocated ____ marriage.
n46ad554529b.x: The Dharmashastras advocated pre-puberty marriage; widows were to stay celibate and svayamvara gave way to arranged marriages.

neb07cba5bfd.s: The largest west-coast port of the Gupta period was:
neb07cba5bfd.x: Bharuch was the largest west-coast port; Ghantasala, Kadura and Chaul also handled foreign trade.

n1f9dbcedc45.s: The gold coins of the Guptas were called:
n1f9dbcedc45.x: Gupta gold coins were dinaras, whose gold content declined in later reigns; copper issues were few and cowries served daily exchange.

n2e0ff11e3ee.s: The Damodarpur copper plates of the Gupta period describe guilds acting as:
n2e0ff11e3ee.x: The Damodarpur plates show guilds functioning as banks; the Mandsaur inscription records the silk-weavers' Sun temple and the Indore plate an oil-men's lamp endowment.

ncdc23c81924.s: The silk weavers' guild of the Mandsaur (Dashpur) inscription migrated to Dashpur from:
ncdc23c81924.x: The guild came from Lata in Gujarat and built a Sun temple at Dashpur; weavers changing professions points to falling silk demand.

n7b19ac907a7.s: Which people disrupted the north-western trade route, contributing to the decline of North Indian trade?
n7b19ac907a7.x: Huna disruption of the north-western route, along with the fall of the West Roman Empire and the Sassanid decline, hurt North Indian trade.

n37633425890.s: Pratishthana, a Gupta-era centre of trade, lay in:
n37633425890.x: Pratishthana lay in the Deccan; Sopara and Barbaricum were in western India.

nc84f5be92ca.s: Fa-Hien's account of his travels is known as the:
nc84f5be92ca.x: Fa-Hien's work is the Fo-kwo-ki (Record of Buddhist Kingdoms); the Si-yu-ki is Hiuen Tsang's.

n11eba5990ff.s: The 'urban decay' interpretation of the post-Gupta period is associated with:
n11eba5990ff.x: R.S. Sharma linked post-Gupta shrinking of towns with a rural, self-sufficient economy and scarcity of gold coins.

nf14da17761a.s: According to Fa-Hien, free hospitals existed at:
nf14da17761a.x: Fa-Hien noted free hospitals at Pataliputra, 20 viharas at Mathura and decay at Kapilavastu, Gaya and Kushinagar.

n3fc754a21d3.s: Ghantasala and Kadura, ports of the Gupta period, were located in present-day:
n3fc754a21d3.x: Ghantasala and Kadura were in Krishna district, while Kalyan and Chaul were on the Konkan coast.

n51e1de6bb00.s: The Narada Smriti lists how many types of slaves?
n51e1de6bb00.x: The Narada Smriti lists 15 types of slaves; in this period Chandalas were outside the varnas while the Shudras' status improved.

nad5593e9b90.s: In the Gupta period, Vidisha was noted for:
nad5593e9b90.x: Vidisha was noted for cloth and ivory; silk weaving was at Lata and Mehrauli is known for the iron pillar.

nee1385d07ef.s: According to Fa-Hien, Chandalas announced their approach by:
nee1385d07ef.x: Fa-Hien says Chandalas lived outside settlements and struck wood to warn others; he also found taxes light and no death penalty.

n0368593c068.s: In the Gupta period, trade with South-East Asia grew through the eastern port of:
n0368593c068.x: South-East Asian trade grew through Tamralipti, but it did not revive the northern economy, which had lost gold and silver inflows.

n9d77881194b.s: Which Gupta-period bodies maintained armed bodies for protection and built rest houses as charity?
n9d77881194b.x: Guilds had armed bodies for protection and built temples, rest houses, assembly halls and gardens as charity.

n3b34289e194.s: In the Gupta period, the marriage gifts that women controlled were called:
n3b34289e194.x: Women lacked general property rights but controlled stridhana; art shows no purdah.

n0672d971d25.s: 'Chinansuka', mentioned in Gupta-period sources, refers to:
n0672d971d25.x: Chinansuka was Chinese silk, showing growing trade with China; the Dharmashastras banned sea travel.

n92cd937a0c3.s: The Gupta silver coin, issued after the conquest of the Western Satraps, was the:
n92cd937a0c3.x: The rupaka was a silver coin for local exchange; the Guptas issued gold dinaras in the largest numbers and few copper coins.

n6a737b2b5d2.s: Which inscription is called the oldest advertisement in the Indian tradition?
n6a737b2b5d2.x: The Dashpur (Mandsaur) inscription, composed by Vatsabhatti, is called the oldest advertisement.

n5447a65466b.s: In ancient Indian trade, a 'Sarthavaha' was a:
n5447a65466b.x: A Sarthavaha was a caravan trader in long-distance trade; the head of a guild was the Sreshthi or Setti.

nfd19bb59f75.s: India's trade with the Eastern Roman Empire continued until about:
nfd19bb59f75.x: Eastern Roman trade lasted until about 550 CE; decline followed in the post-Gupta period, stagnation c. 750-1000 CE, and recovery with the Arab empire.

n2a30e6cb904.s: Castes multiplied in the Gupta period as foreigners and tribes were absorbed into the caste structure, particularly through:
n2a30e6cb904.x: Absorption of foreigners and tribes, especially through land grants, multiplied the sub-castes (jatis).

n5a0abda1f04.s: Which temple belongs to the first stage of Gupta temple architecture, with a flat roof and shallow four-pillared portico?
n5a0abda1f04.x: First-stage temples such as Sanchi Temple 17 and Tigawa have a square sanctum, flat roof and four-pillared portico; Deogarh and Bhitargaon are third-stage.

n7df39cd9aa0.s: The Ajivika sect is associated with:
n7df39cd9aa0.x: The Ajivika sect is associated with Makkhali Gosala; Jainism with Mahavira and the Agamas.

nce7a2d41d0b.s: Tantrism, centred on shakti and open to women and Shudras, began to spread from about the:
nce7a2d41d0b.x: Tantrism spread from about the fifth century and influenced Shaivism, Vaishnavism, Buddhism and Jainism.

n90bbd429e0b.s: Amrakardava, whose Sanchi inscription records a grant to a Buddhist vihara, was an officer of:
n90bbd429e0b.x: Amrakardava, an officer of the Vaishnava king Chandragupta II, gave a grant to the Buddhist vihara at Sanchi, showing Gupta tolerance.

n3cdd42f2562.s: In the Gupta age, religious emphasis shifted from:
o: Sacrifice to temple worship and bhakti
n3cdd42f2562.x: The Gupta shift was from sacrifice to temple and bhakti; iconography of Brahmanical, Jain and Buddhist deities was also standardised.

nca2e2cccc32.s: Who is regarded as the founder of Buddhist logic?
nca2e2cccc32.x: Dinnaga founded Buddhist logic; Asanga was a Yogachara teacher, Vasubandhu wrote the Abhidharmakosa and Buddhaghosa the Visuddhimagga.

n68fb79f0cb1.x: Buddhism lost royal patronage and was persecuted by the Huna ruler Mihirakula.

ncac5e319d69.s: The Ashtanga Marga (eightfold path) is associated with:
ncac5e319d69.x: The Ashtanga Marga is Buddhist; Jainism has the Triratna, Vaishnavism chakra, shankha and Garuda, and Saivism the linga.

n29e97ada736.x: The Guptas patronised Bhagavatism yet were tolerant; Samudragupta let Meghavarman build a monastery at Bodh Gaya.

ne9d543a274a.s: Heliodorus, who set up the Garuda pillar at Besnagar, was the envoy of the Indo-Greek king:
ne9d543a274a.x: Heliodorus, envoy of Antialcidas to the Sunga court of Bhagabhadra, erected the Garuda pillar to Vasudeva and called himself a Bhagavata.

ncb8b142639a.s: Bhagavatism centred on the worship of Vasudeva-Krishna of the ____ clan.
ncb8b142639a.x: Bhagavatism centred on Vasudeva-Krishna of the Vrishni (Satvata) clan; its foundations were karma, bhakti and ahimsa.

nindian-history-51-32.s: The Lingayat sect was founded by:
nindian-history-51-32.x: The Lingayats followed Basava; Lakulisha founded the Pashupata and Matsyendranath and Gorakhnath led the Nathpanth.

nfe03e963530.s: In the doctrine of the Pashupata sect, 'pashu' denotes the:
nfe03e963530.x: In Pashupata doctrine pashu is the individual soul and pati the Supreme soul; the sect, the oldest Shaiva one, was founded by Lakulisha.

n97cf2c68989.s: The earliest example of the Panchayatana plan is the:
n97cf2c68989.x: Panchayatana is a main shrine with four corner shrines, first seen at Deogarh; Bhumara has only two flanking shrines.

n46c1d1c144d.s: In Gupta temple architecture, the raised platform on which the temple stands is called the:
n46c1d1c144d.x: Gupta temples fixed the square garbhagriha, pillared mandapa, pradakshina path and raised jagati platform; the large gopura is a later feature.

n347ad7499e0.s: The Gupta-period Sultanganj Buddha, over two metres high, is made of:
n347ad7499e0.x: The Sultanganj Buddha is a bronze image over two metres high; Gupta stone sculpture grew from the Mathura school.

n1a19e964f87.s: Which Gupta temple has a covered ambulatory and a two-storeyed structure?
n1a19e964f87.x: The Nachna Parvati temple has a covered ambulatory and two storeys; Sanchi 17 has a flat roof, Bhumara flanking shrines and Deogarh a shikhara.

n8e2a14b1c8d.x: The Aryabhatiya dates to 499 CE; Aryabhata held that the Earth is spherical and rotates and gave an accurate value of pi.

n4c3bc2c4f91.s: Ajanta painting, Sarnath sculpture and the first structural temples are cited to call which period a 'Classical Age'?
n4c3bc2c4f91.x: The peak of Sanskrit literature, advances in mathematics and astronomy, Ajanta, Sarnath and the first structural temples mark the Gupta classical age.

n4a311fbca76.s: Which of the following is cited as a criticism of calling the Gupta period a 'Golden Age'?
n4a311fbca76.x: Expansion of vishti, along with land grants, decline of towns and falling status of women, is cited against the Golden Age label.

n7fc0a916f6f.s: The Gwalior inscription, which shows zero as a circle, is dated:
n7fc0a916f6f.x: The Gwalior inscription is of 876 CE; the Sankheda plate is of 594 CE and the Mankani plates of 595-596.

n0570ef0035a.s: How many Buddhist viharas are there at Bagh?
n0570ef0035a.x: Bagh has nine Buddhist viharas; Ellora 1-12 are Buddhist and Udayagiri has nineteen Hindu and one Jain cave.

nd61f819b8d0.s: The Harishena who wrote the Brihatkatha Kosha was a later ____ author, distinct from Samudragupta's court poet.
nd61f819b8d0.x: The Brihatkatha Kosha's Harishena was a later Jain author, different from the Harishena of the Prayaga Prashasti.

n629dd9c3776.s: The Katantra grammar was written by:
n629dd9c3776.x: Sharvavarman wrote Katantra; Amarasimha the Amarakosha, Chandragomin the Chandra Vyakarana and Vararuchi the Prakrit Prakasha.

n8fa1503f9a6.s: The Romaka and Paulisa Siddhantas show ____ influence on Gupta-age science.
n8fa1503f9a6.x: The Romaka and Paulisa Siddhantas reflect Greek input, so Gupta intellectual culture was not free of external influence.

nf93fe528d64.s: The Mehrauli iron pillar was originally set up at:
nf93fe528d64.x: The pillar, now at Mehrauli in Delhi, was originally erected at Udayagiri near Vidisha.

nf34c22e229f.s: Of the twenty Udayagiri caves near Vidisha, how many are Jain?
nf34c22e229f.x: Udayagiri has twenty caves: nineteen Hindu (with Varaha and Shiva images) and one Jain.

ndc2a9ee6d7d.s: The Hitopadesha is a later work based on the:
ndc2a9ee6d7d.x: The Hitopadesha was composed later and based on the Panchatantra.

o: Tempera on dry lime plaster (fresco secco)
nbf58c2cf432.x: Ajanta paintings are tempera on dry lime plaster, with red outlines filled in colour, including lapis-lazuli blue.

n75944ad1c1d.s: The Mother and Child panel at Ajanta is associated with Cave:
n75944ad1c1d.x: The Mother and Child panel is in Cave 17; Padmapani and Vajrapani are Bodhisattvas, and the Mahaparinirvana is a sculpture.

ncf91a1ecc96.x: Hastyayurveda was written by Palakapya, not Dhanvantari.

ne910800832a.x: Vetala Bhatta is linked with Mantrashastra; Dhanvantari with Ayurveda and Vararuchi with Prakrit grammar.

ne6109963735.s: Navanitakam was an ancient Indian medical manual dealing with:
ne6109963735.x: Navanitakam dealt with metallic preparations; physicians used iron and mercury and performed operations such as lithotomy.

nindian-history-6-34.s: The Geet Govind dates to the:
nindian-history-6-34.x: The Geet Govind is a 12th-century work.

n7613ee958fe.x: Shudraka wrote the Mrichchhakatika; Bhasa wrote Charudatta and Vishakhadatta the Devichandraguptam.

n7f50a8a8cfe.s: The Kartikeya (king feeding a peacock) coin type belongs to:
n7f50a8a8cfe.x: The Kartikeya type belongs to Kumaragupta I; the veena-player type is Samudragupta's and archer and lion-slayer types are Chandragupta II's.

n8e8043aa7fa.s: Who, in 629 CE, wrote numbers in decimal place value using a circle for zero?
n8e8043aa7fa.x: Bhaskara I, commentator on the Aryabhatiya, wrote place-value numbers with a circle for zero in 629 CE; Lilavati is by Bhaskara II.

nindian-history-48-10.s: Which physician treated Chandapradyota of Avanti?
nindian-history-48-10.x: Jivaka, physician of Bimbisara, treated Chandapradyota; Charaka is linked with Kanishka and Dhanvantari with Chandragupta II.

necab90582e6.s: The later phase of the Ajanta caves was patronised by the Vakataka king:
necab90582e6.x: Ajanta's later phase was under the Vakataka Harishena; Caves 9 and 10 hold the earliest paintings.

nc45ce0fa426.s: Who improved Aryabhata's sine tables and treated termites as a sign of underground water?
nc45ce0fa426.x: Varahamihira, author of the Panchasiddhantika, Brihat Samhita and Brihat Jataka, did both; the Brahmasphutasiddhanta is Brahmagupta's.

nindian-history-14-12.s: Balaputradeva, who endowed a monastery at Nalanda, was king of:
nindian-history-14-12.x: Balaputradeva of Srivijaya endowed a Nalanda monastery; students also came from China, Tibet and Korea.

nindian-history-12-6.s: The largest hoard of Gupta coins was found at:
nindian-history-12-6.x: The largest Gupta hoard came from Bayana in Bharatpur, Rajasthan; gold coins were Dinaras and silver coins Rupakas.

nindian-history-13-11.s: The Sanskrit drama Malavikagnimitram was written by:
nindian-history-13-11.x: Kalidasa wrote Malavikagnimitram as well as Meghaduta and Kumarasambhavam; Vatsyayana wrote the Kamasutra.

nindian-history-13-12.s: The Buddhacharita and Saundarananda were written by:
nindian-history-13-12.x: Ashvaghosha wrote the Buddhacharita, on the Buddha's life, and the Saundarananda, both Buddhist Sanskrit works.

nb2eaf23e2a7.s: The Mogalrajapuram cave site in Andhra Pradesh is known for five caves and an image of:
nb2eaf23e2a7.x: Mogalrajapuram has five caves and a Nataraja image; Bhairavakonda has eight Kapalika caves.

n694807a30ee.s: Which Navaratna of the traditional list belonged to the sixth century, later than Chandragupta II?
n694807a30ee.x: The Navaratna list is traditional; Varahamihira, for example, belonged to the sixth century, so not all members were contemporaries.

nindian-history-6-33.s: The Sanskrit drama Svapnavasavadattam was written by:

n1f71440c5de.s: Which of the following is one of the five siddhantas summarised in the Panchasiddhantika?
n1f71440c5de.x: The Panchasiddhantika summarises the Surya, Romaka, Paulisa, Vasishtha and Paitamaha siddhantas.

neb3c6808db2.s: Sculptures of the Sarnath school of the Gupta period were carved mainly in:
neb3c6808db2.x: Sarnath sculpture used polished Chunar buff sandstone and avoided heavy ornament.

n94b35c144a4.s: Amarasimha, one of the traditional Navaratnas, was a:
n94b35c144a4.x: Amarasimha was the lexicographer who compiled the Amarakosha; Ayurveda is linked with Dhanvantari.

n6c5f24eaea7.s: The Si-Yu-Ki, a foreign account of Harsha's India, was written by:
n6c5f24eaea7.x: Hiuen Tsang wrote the Si-Yu-Ki; Harshacharita is Bana's Sanskrit biography of Harsha.

n4d7204ae644.s: Harsha's Prayag assembly, at which he gave away his treasury, was held every:
n4d7204ae644.x: The Prayag assembly was held every five years; Hiuen Tsang attended the sixth, and all religions were represented.

nindian-history-45-20.s: Hastimalla was a poet and playwright in which language?
nindian-history-45-20.x: Hastimalla was a Kannada poet and playwright; Kshemendra was the 11th-century Kashmiri Sanskrit poet.

n7c7220ab12f.s: According to Hiuen Tsang, how many times was he robbed in Harsha's otherwise well-governed kingdom?
n7c7220ab12f.x: Hiuen Tsang found light taxes and no revolts, yet was robbed twice; he also saw signs of trade decline.

nindian-history-144-7.x: The Mahamoksha Council met at the Prayagraj Sangam; the Kannauj Assembly was a separate gathering.

nindian-history-144-12.s: Harsha was defeated by Pulakesin II on the banks of the:
nindian-history-144-12.x: Pulakesin II defeated Harsha on the Narmada; Harsha's base was Thanesar and his later capital Kannauj.

nindian-history-46-5.x: Banabhatta wrote the Harshacharita and Kadambari.

nf616454ef6a.s: Grahavarman was a ruler of the:
nf616454ef6a.x: Grahavarman was a Maukhari; Sasanka ruled Gauda, Bhaskaravarman Kamarupa and Dhruvasena II Valabhi.

n278fba82702.s: According to Hiuen Tsang, the premier city of northern India had become:
n278fba82702.x: Hiuen Tsang found that Kannauj, not Pataliputra, was the premier city; he also described Bhinmal and the Multan Sun temple.

nad82bbdd4ec.s: Which source for Harsha's reign bears Harsha's own signature?
nad82bbdd4ec.x: The Banskhera inscription bears Harsha's signature; the Madhuban plate helps with chronology and the Sonpat seal is another inscriptional source.

n3efe87dd6ec.x: The Harsha era began in 606 CE, the year of his accession at 16; 647 CE is the year of his death.

nc7e4c64d18f.s: Prabhavatigupta, whose regency gave the Guptas indirect control of the Deccan, was the daughter of:
nc7e4c64d18f.x: Prabhavatigupta was Chandragupta II's daughter and wife of the Vakataka Rudrasena II.

n775756f31e2.s: In Harsha's time, the head of Nalanda was:
n775756f31e2.x: Silabhadra headed Nalanda in Harsha's time; the institution, founded by Kumaragupta I, was a Mahayana centre.

ne86f0790d97.s: According to Hiuen Tsang, Dhanyakataka had about 20 viharas of which Buddhist sect?
ne86f0790d97.x: Dhanyakataka had about 20 Mahasanghika viharas and Vengi about 20 viharas; Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda were decaying.

nindian-history-46-32.x: Bhavabhuti wrote Mahaviracharitam; Rajasekhara wrote Viddhasalabhanjika and Vishakhadatta the Mudrarakshasa.

nae1ca339f29.x: Harsha was Siladitya and Sakalottarapathanatha; he died in 647 CE without an heir.

n9ee43865a1c.s: In Harsha's administration, Simhanada held the post of:
n9ee43865a1c.x: Simhanada was commander-in-chief; Avanti handled war and peace, Kuntala the cavalry and Skandagupta the elephant force.

nf2ef6234500.s: The Kannauj assembly, held to honour Hiuen Tsang and propagate Mahayana, lasted:
nf2ef6234500.x: The Kannauj assembly lasted 23 days and was followed by violence and an attempt on Harsha's life.

n1230d26c9f4.s: The only Vakataka ruler to assume the title 'Samrat' was:
n1230d26c9f4.x: Pravarasena I, son of Vindhyashakti, alone took the title Samrat and performed Vajapeya and Ashvamedha sacrifices.

n82e47be7834.s: Nalanda provided free boarding for about how many students?
n82e47be7834.x: Nalanda boarded about 10,000 students free; Hiuen Tsang studied and taught there, and Harsha built a multi-storied monastery.

nb9c6a4307ed.s: Which pro-Buddhist measure did Harsha adopt?
o: Making Buddhism the only permitted religion
nb9c6a4307ed.x: Harsha banned animal food and punished killing of living beings, but stayed tolerant and kept patronising Brahmanical scholars.

n5fe371a943f.s: The capital of Shashanka of Gauda was:
n5fe371a943f.x: Shashanka ruled Gauda from Karnasuvarna; Harsha allied against him with Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa.

n63f3a09d1f7.s: Narasimhavarman, praised by Hiuen Tsang, was a ruler of the:
n63f3a09d1f7.x: Hiuen Tsang praised Harsha, Pulakesin II of the Chalukyas and Narasimhavarman of the Pallavas.

nindian-history-46-24.s: Rajasekhara, author of Kavyamimamsa, was a court scholar of the:
nindian-history-46-24.x: Rajasekhara served the Gurjara-Pratiharas Mahendrapala I and Mahipala I.

nindian-history-46-7.s: The Mattavilasa Prahasana was written by:
nindian-history-46-7.x: Mattavilasa Prahasana is by the Pallava king Mahendravarman I; Dandin wrote Dashakumaracharita and Bharavi Kiratarjuniyam.

nindian-history-144-6.s: The Kannauj Assembly of 643 CE was attended by rulers of how many countries?
nindian-history-144-6.x: Rulers of 20 countries, Brahmins, Shramanas and courtiers attended the Kannauj Assembly.

nf54db66fcc4.s: Which Valabhi ruler became Harsha's vassal and married Harsha's daughter?
nf54db66fcc4.x: Dhruvasena II of Valabhi was made Harsha's vassal and married his daughter.

n28ff6d4c52e.s: According to Hiuen Tsang, the Buddhist sites of Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda were:
n28ff6d4c52e.x: Hiuen Tsang found Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda decaying, Sriparvata lacking patronage and some monasteries degenerated.

naea473f4643.s: Before Harsha shifted his capital there, Kannauj was the capital of the:
naea473f4643.x: Thanesar was Harsha's first capital and Kannauj was the Maukhari capital.

n8da16121717.s: In Harsha's fourfold division of revenue, one part was reserved for:
n8da16121717.x: Harsha's revenue went to the king's use, public servants, scholars and religious activities.

nindian-history-1-91.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the tripartite struggle?
o: Govinda III was a Rashtrakuta king.
The Khalimpur inscription records the election of Devapala.
The Sanjan and Radhanpur plates record Govinda III's northern victories.
Nagabhata II was the Gurjara-Pratihara king defeated by Govinda III.
nindian-history-1-91.x: Dharmapala's Khalimpur inscription records the election of Gopala, not Devapala; the other three are correct.

ndd9f13a702a.s: Kannauj gave access to Arabian Sea trade through Gujarat, bypassing the Arab-held:
ndd9f13a702a.x: Kannauj commanded the Doab's agrarian wealth and Arabian Sea trade via Gujarat, bypassing the Arab-held Indus delta.

n17a8bc4c8d8.s: The Rashtrakuta capital during the tripartite struggle was:
n17a8bc4c8d8.x: The Rashtrakutas ruled from Manyakheta in the Deccan; Mihira Bhoja was a Gurjara-Pratihara, not a Pala.

n228624951fd.s: Which Rashtrakuta ruler defeated both Vatsaraja and Dharmapala, then returned south with booty?
n228624951fd.x: Dhruva defeated Vatsaraja and Dharmapala but did not keep northern territory, returning south with booty.

n550c3c502d7.s: Who ousted Chakrayudha, Dharmapala's nominee, from Kannauj?
n550c3c502d7.x: After Vatsaraja and then Dharmapala's nominee Chakrayudha, Nagabhata II ousted Chakrayudha; Mihira Bhoja and Mahendrapala I later held Kannauj.

n08592ade6f0.s: The Somapura Mahavihara was founded by:
n08592ade6f0.x: Dharmapala founded both Vikramashila and Somapura; Gopala built Odantapuri.

ncb520c34425.s: Vikramashila Mahavihara is located at Antichak in which district of Bihar?
ncb520c34425.x: Vikramashila is at Antichak in Bhagalpur district; it had 208 cells and was a Vajrayana centre.

n2445a738333.s: The last strong Pala ruler (c. 1072-1126) was:
n2445a738333.x: Ramapala was the last strong Pala ruler, associated with the Kaivarta revolt, Kamarupa and Kalinga, and Jagaddala.

n4b2e78af92f.s: Dharmapala was defeated by Nagabhata II near:
n4b2e78af92f.x: Dharmapala, who installed Chakrayudha and founded Vikramashila, was defeated by Nagabhata II near Monghyr.

n08dec664b90.s: The Pala ruler Gopala is associated with the construction of:
n08dec664b90.x: Gopala built Odantapuri and displaced the later Guptas of Magadha and the Khadgas of eastern Bengal.

nindian-history-14-11.s: Nalanda, the Buddhist centre of learning in Bihar, was founded in the:
nindian-history-14-11.x: Nalanda was founded in the 5th century AD by the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I.

na0c30f11f9e.s: Under the Palas, which Mahavihara was associated with translating books into Tibetan?
na0c30f11f9e.x: Jagaddala was associated with Tibetan translation, while Buddhist texts were compiled at Nalanda under Dharmapala.

n543271d8c2c.s: Illustrated Buddhist manuscripts of the Pala period were written on:
n543271d8c2c.x: Pala art included bronze and black-stone sculpture and illustrated palm-leaf Buddhist manuscripts.

n1eb8e44ceef.s: In the time of Harsha, Valabhi was known as a centre of:
n1eb8e44ceef.x: Valabhi was a Hinayana centre in Harsha's time, distinct from the Pala Mahaviharas.
